sources.name: Yenko Supercar Registry (yenko.net) - April 2001 Feature Car
sources.says: Yenko ordered 125 Novas (RPO L65 350/250hp, M20, 4.10 12-bolt) then a second batch of 50; COPO 9010 & 9737 replaced the L65 with the 360hp LT-1 from the Z28, plus M21 and F41. 125 + 50 = 175. Yenko stripes/wheels/hood tach added after the factory (likely Hurst).

sources.name: Wikipedia - Chevrolet LT-1
sources.says: In 1970 a Nova could be ordered with the LT-1 via COPO; the 1970 LT-1 was rated 360 hp gross in the Camaro (370 in the Corvette, the same engine). BUT it says only 50 (of 52 Nova COPO LT-1s) became Yenko Deuces, and that Yenko 'converted another 125 L65 Novas into LT-1 Deuces' (175 total).

sources.name: Sports Car Market - 1970 Chevrolet Nova Yenko Deuce profile
sources.type: magazine market profile (editorial analysis of a sale; weaker)
sources.says: Yenko used his Chevrolet connections to get the base engine replaced with the 360-hp LT-1 under COPO 9010; one of 175 built for 1970; LT-1 installed at the factory before the cars reached Yenko.

disagreements: Factory-installed engine for all 175: yenko.net and Sports Car Market say COPO 9010/9737 covered both batches (factory LT-1). Wikipedia says only 50 were COPO LT-1 cars and Yenko converted the other 125 from L65 Novas. Wikipedia's 52-unit Nova COPO LT-1 figure has no clear citation; the registry is the more specific and authoritative source.
COPO number: the registry lists two COPOs, 9010 and 9737 (9737 was a Yenko/sport-trim COPO also used on 1969 Camaros). The engine COPO is 9010.
HP: everyone agrees on 360 hp gross (the same engine was rated 370 hp in the Corvette).
Count: everyone agrees on 175 (registry: 125 + 50; Chevy Hardcore and others: 122 four-speeds + 53 automatics).
conclusion: With NHRA and Chevy Hardcore, there are now two more independent sources (the Yenko registry and Wikipedia) plus a weaker third (Sports Car Market). All confirm a 1970 Nova Yenko Deuce with the COPO 9010 LT-1 350 rated 360 hp gross, 175 built. Safe page wording: 'COPO 9010 LT-1 350, 360 hp (gross), 175 built for Yenko Chevrolet.' Hedge 'factory-built' slightly: the registry and SCM say the LT-1 was installed at the factory under COPO, but Wikipedia says 125 of the 175 were Yenko conversions.
